text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong gives account of strained ties between Singapore and Malaysia and offers framework for wider cooperation.
- Goh outlines vision for Singapore in 21st century and calls for change in mindset, placing people ahead of material progress.
- Hollywood-style parade will mark 30 years of military national service in Singapore.
- Big crush develops at Registry of Marriages as couples book wedding date to avoid paying Singapore $5,000 deposit for Housing Board flats.
- Emporium Holdings group confirms negotiating to sell majority stake to trendy Hong Kong retailer Theme International Holdings.
- Thai baht rockets to 13-year high in offshore markets as speculators scramble to scoop up baht while selling U.S. dollars heavily to cover short positions.
- Parkway Holdings shares fall as posturing continues over whether controlling Tan family would sell its 21 percent stake to DBS Land.
- Customs and Excise Department makes surprise visit to 20 car dealers, most understood to be parallel importers, and seize files and documents.

- Share prices of Sing Tao Holdings and associate Culturecom Holdings largely unaffected despite news of arrest of six people in connection with scheme in which Sing Tao's English-language Hong Kong newspaper allegedly inflated circulation figures.
- In what may be prelude to other deals, Ong Beng Seng's Hotel Properties Ltd ropes two large Hong Kong-listed groups into Italian hotel venture.
- Listed property group Liang Court Holdings feels its shares are undervalued, given its minimal exposure to the Singapore property market.
